# Qi2 vs. Qi2.2 vs. MagSafe

**Qi2** is the Wireless Power Consortium's (WPC) open standard. It adds a magnetic ring that aligns the phone and charger, and it tops out at 15W. It's based on Apple's MagSafe technology, which Apple contributed to ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/news/708060/qi-2-2-certification-25w-wpc-belkin-anker-ugreen-aukey)). The magnets improve efficiency and speed and make placement easier ([WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/)).

**Qi2.2** (technically Qi v2.2.1, branded "Qi2 25W") is the same magnetic design at up to 25W. The WPC says that's nearly 70% more power, enough to charge a phone from 0 to 50% in about 30 minutes ([WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/)). The first certified products appeared in July 2025.

**MagSafe** is Apple's own branding and certification program. Per [Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html):
- Certified MagSafe chargers include an NFC antenna so the iPhone can identify them. They also have a magnetometer to prevent compass interference.
- Apple's current MagSafe Charger is also certified for Qi2 25W, so the lines have largely merged.
- Uncertified "MagSafe-compatible" chargers are usually just magnets plus 7.5W charging.

## Speeds by iPhone
Per [Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-ie/105047), with Apple's MagSafe Charger and a 30W or higher adapter:
- **25W:** iPhone 17 series, 18 Pro models, 16 Plus and 16 Pro Max.
- **22.5W:** iPhone 16 and 16 Pro.
- **20W:** iPhone Air.
- **15W:** iPhone 15 and earlier (back to 12), and the 17e.
- The iPhone 16e has no magnetic charging.

## Android
Android support is thin ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/gadgets/939362/best-magsafe-qi2-2-batteries-power-banks)):
- The Pixel 10, 10 Pro and 10 Pro Fold support Qi2 at 15W.
- The Pixel 10 Pro XL supports Qi2.2 at 25W.
- Samsung's Galaxy lineup is "Qi2 Ready" and needs a magnetic case.

## Which to buy
Any Qi2.2-certified charger gives the same 25W as Apple's, and Qi2 chargers are fine if 15W is enough. Look for the Qi2 logo, which only certified products can display. You can check a product in the [WPC database](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/).

If you want the simplest option, [Apple's MagSafe Charger (2 m) is $49](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m?fnode=7120d2e211c5d2008372acfadfa9b649c5ec92879b07e2f040e38952fcd8be0794ade18a93d927b4c96c7a13cda2597927c0814a65dc0189e774b77c7fdb7e748fe7efe26c0c6c21f59929ac37012aa0ac916746c2f56a8e6448ccdb97e7d384&fs=s%3Dnewest%26fh%3D8e12f5%252B81eaf8). A 1 m version is also sold, listed around $39 by Macworld. The adapter is sold separately, and Apple recommends its 30W USB-C adapter for full 25W speed.

If you want an all-in-one stand for iPhone, Apple Watch and AirPods, the [ESR CryoBoost 3-in-1 Qi2.2 stand](https://dealectric.com/esr-cryoboost-3-in-1-qi2-2-25w-stand) is $99.99, and a listing says code PARTNER18 takes $17.99 off. That's an affiliate link, so the site earns a commission if you buy. Its listing also notes that 25W applies only to certain iPhones, and that the stand includes a 50W adapter.

What phone do you have? I can narrow this down once I know.
